# Native signed productivity vectors

This is a prospective engine fixture, not a native result, reporter-save reproduction or full Cerys test. The real MIR mod initializes and handles configuration/research events normally. The scenario neither imports MIR runtime modules nor reads its saved ledger. Its only research setup is explicitly labelled recursive finite prerequisites; four MIR main levels and the pending partial must come from a real lab consuming all four required packs.

Package `data.lua`, `data-final-fixes.lua`, `contract.lua`, the unmodified `cerys-technology-first45.lua`, `Cerys-LICENSE.txt` and the selected metadata as `info.json` in the tiny fixture mod. **Do not package `control.lua` as a mod script.** Copy that one shared actor into the scenario's `control.lua`; its `__level__` configuration callback records entry before MIR. All six metadata files use the same data/actor bodies. Keep player packages and original saves immutable; a controller must bind exact engine, package, scenario, fixture/archive-member and save hashes separately.

The exact official closure is Base, Space Age, Quality and Elevated Rails at the declared engine version, plus Recycler on 2.1.23, MIR and this fixture only. Require map research price multiplier 1 and `mir-prefer-this-mod-for-competing-techs=true`. This preference does not itself expose MIR's private Space Age identity: the fixture explicitly gives that same authored main a neutral test mask from its three validated native signed-holder components. It never changes its `8000*2^(L-1)` formula, 60-second unit, four science ingredients or prerequisites. The stock transport must contain exactly LDS, casting LDS and Scrap before any aliases exist.

The real upstream loop adds the nuclear Scrap and processing-unit aliases to native public and private technologies. Ninety-five additional Scrap aliases are explicitly synthetic. All are defined after MIR's recipe collection, so they create no new MIR descriptors. The public Scrap reference and each Scrap carrier consequently have exactly 97 components; the F1 main has those 97 plus LDS/casting. Main and reference vectors, every carrier sign/count/flag, and every named force recipe's actual `productivity_bonus` are checked. Complete vectors are also emitted in the raw frame without inventing the absent 2.0 `hidden` effect field.

| Fixture | Main mask | Required checkpoint before continuation | Ordinary work and saved result |
|---|---|---|---|
| F0, 0.1.0 | Public LDS/casting; Scrap excluded | Zero main/reference/carriers and zero bonuses after real MIR init | Two ordinary main levels, 24,000 of each pack charged; Scrap 0 and LDS/casting .2; `native-vector-f0.zip` |
| F1, 0.2.0 | Public LDS/casting and full Scrap vector | Negative Scrap 2; Scrap 0 and LDS/casting .2; `native-vector-f1-negative.zip` | Server `continue`: one ordinary main level, then genuinely lab-earned current partial in [.2,.3) with unrelated sentinel second in queue; Scrap .1, LDS/casting .3; `native-vector-f1-pending.zip` |
| F2, 0.3.0 | Empty, hidden, disabled prototype; original unit retained | Positive Scrap 1 and LDS/casting 3; exact pre-MIR native pending/queue/unit and every incoming force flag retained; `native-vector-f2-positive.zip` | Server `continue`: finish that one paid partial ordinarily; positive Scrap 2 and LDS/casting 4; 120,000 of each pack charged cumulatively; `native-vector-final.zip` |

The exact server command at each declared F1/F2 checkpoint is `/mir-native-credit-vectors continue`. It cannot run in any other phase or from a player. Each checkpoint stops the native lab, writes its own immutable expected frame and requests a server save. A supervising owner must wait for the corresponding marker **and closed valid ZIP**, then protect a physically distinct copy. F1/F2 pre-MIR raw frames distinguish engine prototype-change effects from MIR reconciliation; they are not used to infer old paid rights. On F2, preserve every actual pre-MIR force flag exactly. This native-owner historical holder is outside the authored-generated lifecycle declarations; its hidden/disabled prototype does not authorize forcing an existing force flag false. Whether the engine permits the already queued retired main to finish remains a native gate; no fixture level/enable/partial setter bypasses it. A work-frame refusal emits its exact expected/actual observations before the unchanged strict assertion.

The smallest main progression schedule is three server processes (F0, F1, F2) plus two one-update immutable cold reads of the final save. The F1 negative and F2 positive checkpoints can each receive separate two-cold checks before a fresh continuing server if required by the governing packet; they already have distinct save names and a server-only continuation. Each cold must start from an identical protected save hash, run exactly one update, produce `kind=cold` and match its entire stored native frame without feeding/requeueing/saving or changing fixture storage. An owner must independently prove same save bytes, exact cold update/exit, process bounds and control/archive restoration. Fixture markers alone provide no such authority.

The test lab has a durable test-only void energy source and speed 100001. Entity placement and science supply are administrative, tracked separately from native consumption. The actor stops/feeds only through the portable read/write `LuaEntity.disabled_by_script` field; it never writes `active`, which is read-only in the pinned 2.1.23 SDK (and deprecated for writing in 2.0.77). It preserves original main costs/time/science, stops on every ordinary completion, and requeues only on a later tick. It accepts either native completed-N/true or advanced-(N+1)/false representation through effective completed-count arithmetic. Scripted main grants, extra completions, missing consumption, wrong vector tails/signs/flags, changed partial/queue, wrong phase/tuple, and changed or premature colds refuse. Native carrier-copy events are excluded from ordinary counts only inside explicit reconciliation windows and must lead to the exact expected signed frame.

The public Scrap reference and unrelated sentinel have one saved native status baseline captured from the genuinely uninvested F0 world. Their level/researched/enabled/visibility/saved-progress fields must stay exact before and after configuration, throughout ordinary work and at every checkpoint/cold. Later entries/saves cannot silently replace this baseline. Intentional signed carrier changes and the declared main retirement remain separate from these immutable native statuses.

`upstream.json` identifies the original complete 3,885-byte member and unchanged first 45-line loop by SHA256. That excerpt comes from Cerys 4.24.16 by its upstream authors, under the included complete CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license text (only its extra empty EOF line is omitted); see the [upstream repository](https://github.com/danielmartin0/Cerys-Moon-of-Fulgora). Its processing alias branch is retained verbatim rather than edited away. This fixture does not bundle the Cerys mod or assert that it caused the reporter's 97-effect state.

Run the HostControls `-Plan` first, then `python -B tests/test_native_credit_vector_fixture.py --lua-runtime-dir <pinned Lua52 directory>`. Host doubles test observer refusal paths and both completion representations; a separate control runs the actual complete `runtime.native_credits` module through all three family masks on both numeric targets. Neither is an engine, physical-production, native save/cold, performance, multiplayer or reporter-repair verdict. Root owns driver registration, controller construction, actual dispatch, independent review and any resulting claim.
